facts.text: ContinuousInsertionRandomizedMarkerEnv-v1 is registered with the entry point envs.peg_insertion:ContinuousInsertionSimGymRandomizedPointFLowEnv
The environment base class ContinuousInsertionSimEnv derives from gymnasium's gym.Env
The action space is Box(low=-1, high=1, shape=(3,), dtype=np.float32), a three-element action
The constructor requires step_penalty, final_reward and max_action; max_steps defaults to 15
step increments the episode counter, multiplies the action by max_action, and returns observation, reward, terminated, truncated and info
The action is clipped to +-max_action; its in-plane components are rotated by the current offset angle and added to the x and y offset, and its third component is added to the theta offset
The error-too-large thresholds are 12 on the x offset, 12 on the y offset and 15 on the theta offset, compared with a 1e-5 tolerance
The reward is the decrease of the evaluated offset error minus step_penalty; an error-too-large step adds -2*step_penalty*(max_steps-steps)+step_penalty and a success adds final_reward
The episode truncates when the elapsed steps reach max_steps and terminates on error_too_large or is_success
The registered class's default observation holds gt_offset (three float32 values) and marker_flow of shape (2, 2, 128, 2) float32; render_rgb defaults to False
reset accepts offset, seed and peg_idx and returns the observation with an empty info dictionary
seed() sets numpy's global random generator with np.random.seed
The registered subclass reads kwargs['params'].tac_sensor_meta_file before the superclass constructor, so a params object is mandatory
The upstream training configuration sets step_penalty 1, final_reward 10, max_action [2.0, 2.0, 4.0] and max_steps 8 for this environment
The training script creates the environment with gym.make(env_name, device=wp_device, **env_args), so the constructor arguments come from the caller

determinism.notes: the fake seeds its generator from reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1, so a seed repeats its trajectory; the upstream reset accepts a seed argument but does not call seed(), so this claim covers the fake backend only and was not established on the upstream environment

gaps: the fake backend is a kinematic/analytic stand-in: it integrates the commanded offset, rotated by the current theta, and applies the upstream error, truncation and reward rules; it does not simulate SAPIEN/IPC contacts, elastic sensor deformation, marker motion, peg/hole geometry or success detection

the upstream environment is a SAPIEN + SapienIPC GPU simulation (envs/peg_insertion.py imports sapien; README.md:51 requires SapienIPC); it was neither imported nor run here, and the sim backend was not run
the marker_flow observation is a zero array of the real (2, 2, 128, 2) shape: the fake computes no tactile marker flow, so that field carries no information
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and clock lockstep
timestep_ms 0: one tick is one environment step; the upstream runs a number of IPC substeps that depends on the action and params.sim_time_step, so no fixed physics interval per tick is claimed
the upstream registration supplies no constructor arguments and the registered subclass requires a params object (envs/peg_insertion.py:763), so gymnasium.make(env_id) alone cannot build it
the fake's initial offset draw, max_action, max_steps, step_penalty and final_reward are placeholder test data, not a bound of the upstream environment
snapshot and restore are not offered: the upstream class exposes no get_state/set_state

safe_state.description: the simulation is latched: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state stays readable
